resources.string: No nodes yet. Add the address of the Pi that runs Node Talker.
Keep the screen on while a node is open
Type the Pi\'s address: letters, digits, dots, dashes or an IP address.
The port must be a number from 1 to 65535.
Certificate forgotten. The next connection asks again.

%1$s uses its own certificate (made on the Pi), so Android can't vouch for it.

SHA-256 fingerprint:
%2$s

To check it on the Pi:
openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256 -in /etc/asl_dvs/nodetalker_tls/cert.pem

Trust it only if it matches. The app remembers it and warns you if it ever changes.

%1$s now shows a different certificate than the one you trusted.

It changes if Node Talker made a new one (for example after a reinstall). If you did not expect that, someone may be in the way: cancel.

New SHA-256 fingerprint:
%2$s
The node\'s certificate could not be read, so the connection was stopped.
Certificate not trusted, so the page was not opened.
No browser app was found to open %1$s
Microphone permission was refused, so this node can\'t use the microphone.

Page audio: as in a browser (use it if app audio sounds bad)
